question: What nationality is the director of the film that the actor who played Jaime Lannister appeared in for Fox in 2009?

supporting_docs.title: Nikolaj Coster-Waldau
supporting_docs.text: Nikolaj Coster-Waldau is a Danish actor who played Jaime Lannister in Game of Thrones and appeared in the 2009 Fox television film Virtuality.

supporting_docs.title: Virtuality (film)
supporting_docs.text: Virtuality is a 2009 American television film that aired on Fox, starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau.

question: Which country is home to both the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre Museum?

supporting_docs.title: Eiffel Tower
supporting_docs.text: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris, France, on the Champ de Mars.

supporting_docs.title: Louvre
supporting_docs.text: The Louvre is the world's most-visited museum, located in Paris, France.

question: In what year did the scientist who discovered the photoelectric effect's theoretical explanation win his Nobel Prize?

supporting_docs.title: Albert Einstein
supporting_docs.text: Albert Einstein developed the theoretical explanation of the photoelectric effect, for which he won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

supporting_docs.title: Photoelectric effect
supporting_docs.text: The photoelectric effect was explained theoretically by Albert Einstein in 1905, work later recognized by the Nobel committee.

question: What language was created by the person who first released it in 1991?

supporting_docs.title: Guido van Rossum
supporting_docs.text: Guido van Rossum is a Dutch programmer who created the Python programming language, first releasing it in 1991.

supporting_docs.title: Python (programming language)
supporting_docs.text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language first released in 1991.

question: Which mountain range contains the peak that straddles the border between Nepal and Tibet?

supporting_docs.title: Mount Everest
supporting_docs.text: Mount Everest straddles the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, and is part of the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.

supporting_docs.title: Himalayas
supporting_docs.text: The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau, containing Mount Everest.

question: What play, written by the author of Macbeth, features a prince of Denmark?

supporting_docs.title: William Shakespeare
supporting_docs.text: William Shakespeare wrote both Macbeth and Hamlet, among many other plays, in the late 16th and early 17th centuries.

supporting_docs.title: Hamlet
supporting_docs.text: Hamlet is a tragedy by William Shakespeare about Prince Hamlet of Denmark.

question: In what U.S. state did the Wright brothers make their first successful powered flight?

supporting_docs.title: Wright brothers
supporting_docs.text: The Wright brothers made the first successful sustained flights of a powered aircraft on December 17, 1903, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

supporting_docs.title: Kitty Hawk
supporting_docs.text: Kitty Hawk is a town in North Carolina known as the site of the Wright brothers' first flight.

question: Who won a Nobel Prize in a different scientific field than the one she first won it in, eight years later?

supporting_docs.title: Marie Curie
supporting_docs.text: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and, eight years later in 1911, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

supporting_docs.title: Nobel Prize
supporting_docs.text: Marie Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

question: Which ocean, bordered by the Arctic Ocean to its north, is both the largest and deepest on Earth?

supporting_docs.title: Pacific Ocean
supporting_docs.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions, extending from the Arctic Ocean in the north to the Southern Ocean in the south.

supporting_docs.title: Ocean
supporting_docs.text: Earth's five oceans include the Pacific, which is both the largest by area and the deepest.

question: What wall, whose fall in 1989 symbolized the end of the Cold War, once divided a German city?

supporting_docs.title: Berlin Wall
supporting_docs.text: The Berlin Wall divided Berlin from 1961 until it fell on November 9, 1989, symbolizing the end of the Cold War.

supporting_docs.title: Cold War
supporting_docs.text: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 is widely seen as a symbolic end to the Cold War era.

question: Which country gifted a statue to the United States that was dedicated in 1886?

supporting_docs.title: Statue of Liberty
supporting_docs.text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France to the United States, dedicated on October 28, 1886.

supporting_docs.title: Franco-American relations
supporting_docs.text: France's gift of the Statue of Liberty in 1886 remains a lasting symbol of French-American friendship.

question: What class of animal, which breathes through gills, includes sharks?

supporting_docs.title: Shark
supporting_docs.text: Sharks are a group of elasmobranch fish that breathe through gills and do not nurse their young with milk.

supporting_docs.title: Elasmobranchii
supporting_docs.text: Elasmobranchii is a subclass of fish that includes sharks, rays, and skates.
